arn:aws:dynamodb:us-east-1:000000000000:.note: Retained AWS-managed SYSTEM backup. Manual removal was not retried: sequence 160 established AWS rejects SYSTEM deletion. Automatic expiration has not been verified.

findings.observation: Both continuous-backup operations returned TableNotFoundException for the missing name. DescribeContinuousBackups also returned TableNotFoundException immediately after successful CreateTable. The table subsequently became ACTIVE, and a separate continuous-backup description reported ContinuousBackupsStatus ENABLED with PITR DISABLED. The disabled no-op and first enable both succeeded; no ContinuousBackupsUnavailableException was observed in this sample.

While PITR was DISABLED, PointInTimeRecoveryDescription contained only PointInTimeRecoveryStatus. EarliestRestorableDateTime, LatestRestorableDateTime, RecoveryPeriodInDays and PointInTimeRecoveryWindowDays were absent. ContinuousBackupsStatus remained ENABLED.

Enabling with retention omitted produced RecoveryPeriodInDays 35 and PointInTimeRecoveryWindowDays 35. Both restore bounds were 1789743996.0. After a deliberate 12-second wait, enabled no-ops with retention omitted and explicitly 35 preserved both exact bounds in update responses and subsequent descriptions.

Changing requested retention from 35 to 1 to 7 was reflected by both RecoveryPeriodInDays and PointInTimeRecoveryWindowDays in update responses and following descriptions, without changing either restore bound. Omitting retention while already enabled at 7 retained 7, including the description after a deliberate 10-second wait.

Retention 0 and 36 returned ValidationException with respective >=1 and <=35 constraints. Empty specification, missing/null enabled field, and missing/null specification returned ValidationException for the required member. Retention string seven returned SerializationException with Message STRING_VALUE cannot be converted to Integer.

The raw JSON enabled value string yes was accepted with Success while PITR was already ENABLED at retention 7. The response and later description remained ENABLED at 7 with unchanged bounds. This does not establish general string-to-boolean conversion behavior.

Disabling removed retention and restore-bound fields; repeating disable preserved that shape. After an 8-second disabled wait, re-enabling with retention 3 returned and subsequently described both retention fields as 3, with both restore bounds reset from 1789743996.0 to 1789744035.0. An additional 8-second wait left those new bounds unchanged.

Cleanup disabled PITR and separately observed DISABLED before DeleteTable. DescribeTable then returned ResourceNotFoundException. BackupType ALL inventories before deletion and twice after deletion had BackupSummaries []; no backup was discovered or needed deletion.

limitations: A sampled transition is not a timing guarantee.

The deletion-disable follow-up observed ContinuousBackupsUnavailableException after the source reached ACTIVE, followed by continuous backups DISABLED during deletion. The repeated experiment waited for successful enablement before testing disablement; initial continuous-backup readiness and its timing are independent of table ACTIVE.
The first post-update descriptions already matched the requested settings; asynchronous propagation latency, latest-restorable advancement cadence, and long-lived no-op behavior are not established.
Sequences 1-53 exercise control-plane behavior only. The follow-up SYSTEM backup experiment exercises RestoreTableFromBackup and actual item recovery, not historical RestoreTableToPointInTime.

The SYSTEM backup expiry observed at retention 1 is one day after creation, despite documentation describing 35-day system retention. Other retention values and actual automatic expiration were not sampled.
Short retention observations cannot establish history expiration after whole days.

systemDeletionExperiment.authorization: Follow-up assignment deliberately deletes this owned source while PITR is enabled to observe native SYSTEM backup creation and restore; all other owned tables are disabled before cleanup deletion.

observations.observation: Restored items equal the strongly consistent pre-deletion source items including the post-enable replacement, deletion and insert.

Deleting the owned source while PITR was ENABLED at RecoveryPeriodInDays 1 created an AVAILABLE SYSTEM backup named stackd-ddb-pitr-system-74ae149b8a5832-source$DeletedTableBackup. BackupCreationDateTime 1789744434.369 and BackupExpiryDateTime 1789830834.369 differ by exactly 86400 seconds. This is the observed native expiry, not the documentation's generic 35-day statement.

SYSTEM and ALL ListBackups filters returned the same one backup; USER returned BackupSummaries []. DescribeBackup retained PROVISIONED 2/2 throughput and pk HASH/sk RANGE schema, SourceTableFeatureDetails {}, ItemCount 0, TableSizeBytes 0 and BackupSizeBytes 0 despite the actual three-item source scan.

RestoreTableFromBackup initially returned CREATING with RestoreSummary.RestoreInProgress true, source table/backup ARNs, and RestoreDateTime 1789744434.369. The restored table later reached ACTIVE; the ACTIVE response omitted RestoreSummary. Its strongly consistent scan returned Count 3 and ScannedCount 3, exactly the pre-deletion items: replaced alpha with counter 42, surviving gamma, inserted delta, and no deleted beta. Restored PITR was DISABLED.

Both source and restored table absence were verified. Restored PITR DISABLED was verified before its deletion. DeleteBackup returned ValidationException: User is not allowed to delete the system backup; it will automatically expire on 2026-09-19T15:13:54.369Z. The retained AVAILABLE SYSTEM backup was described and listed after rejection; its absence was not claimed.

retainedManagedBackups.documentation: AWS documents SYSTEM deleted-table backups retained 35 days at no additional cost; actual expiry is retained in the native description.
retainedManagedBackups.costBasis: The linked AWS documentation describes SYSTEM deleted-table backup retention at no additional cost; billing was not measured.
